tickets.body:
As it stands our calendar logging is still woefully inadequate.

For example, we had a case recently whereby cancel on policy was deleting events in the calendar but was not telling us about it, it was until we saw the fields on the session that we knew that's likely what happened.

Another common example are coaches complaining that events randomly go missing on their calendar.

Another example is a coach says we allow double booking with a blocked external event. We do not have trace of exactly what her calendar looked like then and how our conflict handler responded to allow us to track that and see if something is wrong.

And a last example is: I scheduled an event for 12pm but it says it conflicted with a 10am event, omg you keep messing it up.

This ticket is about solving that so we can debug stuff better.

This rewrite will involve three collections:

- cronjob_tasks
- callback_logs
- dcoach_calendar_event
- action_logs

## cornjob_tasks tasks:

- [ ] All activities on the calendar should place a row into the cronjob_tasks collection
    - [ ] This includes even the full sync within the cronjob which doesn't right now
    - [ ] And cancel policy which also seems to not
- [ ] See if anything else can be saved to help us, like:
    - [ ] calendar ID might help a lot
    - [ ] specific integration ID used
- [ ] The cronjob_task collection needs totally redoing from the ground up.
    - [ ] We need a proper schema that can actually help us identify and diagnose issues
    - [ ] I would like to also see the collection renamed to something more fitting its true purpose like "calendar_sync_logs"

## callback_logs

- [ ] it would be good if we could save a history of associated events for this callback
    - [ ] for google this will just be all events in last 15 mins, cut down to maybe ID, title, startsAt
    - [ ] for outlook this will be the specific event
        - [ ] for deletes we cannot get anything but the ID
- [ ] I even wonder if there is a way to incorporate this into the cornjob_tasks table so we can just get a history of all changes to a client calendar, but that is a maybe and up for discussion as to how easy

## dcoach_calendar_event

This one is a fun one

- [ ] We need to start recording the results of our system against events:
    - [ ] The full results of the conflict handler
        - [ ] This includes both local and remote conflicts in simplified fashion
        - [ ] We ned to know if calendars were not queries cos they were turned off or disabled
        - [ ] We need all fields of the conflict handler checker in the table
- [ ] next to external event ID it would be nice to include a calendar ID or integration ID or both

## action_logs

We ned to start logging failed event creations.

- [ ] Basically add a new event of SESSION_ADDED_CONFLICT
    - [ ] The event itself will be like the calendar event but it will save every time the user gets a response from our conflict handler.

We can then use this to debug the common issue of "why won't this work"

## API response changes

One more bit here is the actual calendar APIs itself.

- [ ] The coach calendar API should include a field for all the events deleted cos they are duped by delenta events
- [ ] Google especially should include a list of deleted events as well (you cant for ical and outlook)

This will make some debugging easier when a coach says that a delenta event is missing cos then we can check the calendar page instantly on the spot instead of having to run a command to do it
tickets.title: Improve calendar logging

### Description:
When a coach has both Free Session buffer settings (e.g. 15 minutes before and after) and External Events buffer settings (e.g. 30 minutes before and after) configured, creating a Free Session currently applies the External Events buffer instead of the Free Session buffer.

This behaviour is confusing because users would expect the buffer configured specifically for Free Sessions to be applied when booking a free session.

### Expected Behaviour:

Free Session bookings should apply the Free Session buffer settings.
External Events buffer settings should only apply to external calendar events (or the intended event type).
If the current behaviour is intentional, the UI or documentation should clearly explain which buffer takes precedence to avoid confusion.

### Reason for Clarification:
It is currently unclear which buffer configuration has priority when multiple buffer settings are configured, leading to unexpected booking availability and potential confusion for coaches.

tickets.body: **Background / Problem Statement** Currently, ACH (Automated Clearing House) transfers configured in Stripe cannot be executed through the platform. This limitation forces users—especially B2B coaches—to rely on card payments, resulting in significantly higher transaction fees. **Example Impact:** - ACH transaction (~$10,368) → approx. $5 fee - Card transaction → approx. $300+ fee **Requirement Description** Enable support for ACH payments via Stripe within the platform, allowing coaches and clients to process bank transfers directly through the system. **Key Functional Requirements** **ACH Payment Option** - The system should allow clients to select ACH (bank transfer) as a payment method where Stripe supports it. - Display ACH as an option alongside card payments during checkout. **Stripe Integration** - Leverage existing Stripe capabilities for ACH debit. - Ensure compatibility with Stripe’s ACH flow (including bank verification if required). **Transaction Handling** - Payments should be processed and tracked similarly to card payments. - Support statuses such as: - Pending (ACH processing delay) - Completed - Failed **UI/UX Considerations** - Clearly indicate that ACH payments may take longer to process than card payments. - Display estimated processing time to users. **Coach Visibility** - Coaches should be able to: - View ACH transactions in reports - Identify the payment method used (ACH vs Card) **Error Handling** - Proper messaging if: - ACH is not supported for a user/region - Bank verification fails - Payment is declined **Non-Functional Requirements** - Ensure compliance with Stripe and banking regulations. - Maintain secure handling of bank account data (no storage on platform if handled by Stripe). - Performance should not degrade existing payment workflows. **Acceptance Criteria** - The user can complete a payment using ACH via Stripe - ACH option appears only where supported - The transaction is recorded correctly in the system - Fees are significantly lower compared to card payments - Proper status updates (pending → completed/failed) are shown - Coaches can view ACH payments in their dashboard/reporting
tickets.title: Support ACH Payments via Stripe Integration

tickets.body:
If a folder is copied into another folder that is already shared with the same folder, it can create a recursive copy loop. This loop negatively affects the performance of the search function.


Plan
----------------
```
When copying a folder (target folder) into the ABC folder, we should first check whether the ABC folder is
already shared with the target folder. If it already exists, we should show a message like the following:

“The ABC folder is already shared with the target folder.
You can continue copying without the ABC folder or stop the process.”

Implementation Logic:

1. Get all shared (shortcut) folder IDs of the ABC folder.
2. Get all nested folder IDs inside the ABC folder.
3. Check whether any shortcut ID matches the nested folders list of the ABC folder.
4. If a match exists: 
  -  Show the warning message with next action options.
  -  If the user chooses Continue:
       -  Remove the ABC folder from the copy list.
       -  Copy the remaining folders only.
   -  if not:
      -  just copy
```

tickets.body:
Currently an Admin/Super Admin/ Coach_Admins are unable to have full control of all folders created within their team. 

Currently only the coach / admin who uploads the file can delete the file. This should not be the case. Admin should have full access rights to all folders and files they see from the team portal resources page. 

Admin should be able to : 

- [ ] Delete, Move, Rename and Upload files to all client shared folders, group folders and the team folder. 

- [ ] The team member who uploads file or creates the folder should have full access rights to the file/folder. 
- [ ] In the case of client shared folders, the primary coach/owner of the client should also have full access to modify the folder and its contents (copy, rename, move within the shared folder, delete etc) 

- [ ] These permissions should apply regardless of the place they upload/modify the files or folders from. As currently they are able to do the same actions from resources and contacts/ CRM page. 

No changes necessary within the team folder. The permission on that folder works fine.

Currently we don't send an Outlook or ICal invites for group sessions and therefore there is no updated invite when rescheduling a group event on these two calendar integrations. 
The reason for this is because Outlook and ICal events make the full attendee list visible on the invite, which is a problem for coaches who are trying to protect their client's private information. 

The solution is to attach the ics as a 7bit encode file embedded into the Delenta Session email to replicate the invite that google etc(removing the attendee lists) and send to clients on scheduling, rescheduling or cancelling a group event. This will avoid clients having to manually add the group sessions via the ADD TO CAL function on Delenta emails. 

Acceptance Criteria:

- [x] Ability for clients to receive outlook and ICal ics files for their group sessions so they can be add to their personal calendars. 
- [x]  The attendee list on these invites should not be visible to all clients of the group. 
- [x] An updated ics file should be sent for Reschedules and cancelations.

> Hi team,

> I am writing this email in connection with potential vulnerabilities found on your website. I work as a security researcher and keep track of vulnerabilities in websites. Sadly, your website has some alarming vulnerabilities that would prove detrimental if exploited correctly.

> 
> Vulnerable Path: https://app.delenta.com/coach/sign-up/confirmation

> I have found that the name field is not sanitizing data properly. While we sign up for an account we can save the URL as a name. Now an attacker can use this as a scam for victims.

> 2) In the name field put any URL like [www.evil.com](http://www.evil.com/)

> 4) Try to log in from different browsers, and you will receive a notification from babble.
> 5) Visit your email box and check that email, you will find a malicious hyperlink in that email.

> 
> Proof of Concept:
> image.png
> Impact:
> This can be used by attackers to scam victims Because attackers can access this page and can enter the victim's email with a malicious URL in the name field. When the victim receives the email, he will be scammed. The result of this feature can be more dangerous.
> 
> Reference:
> https://hackerone.com/reports/158554
> 
> I'd be more than happy to assist you with anything regarding the issue.
